profile.size: Can reach at least 48 inches and 79 lb; sexual maturity is reported around 19 inches for males and 21.5 inches for females. These are maximum/biological reference values, not typical catch sizes.
profile.diet: Benthic feeder that roots through sand and seagrass flats for crabs, shrimp, mollusks and other crustaceans; also takes polychaetes, small fishes and other invertebrates.
profile.behavior: Uses shallow sandy and seagrass flats and intertidal areas to forage, often moving onto flats with incoming tides from adjacent channels and basins. Smaller fish commonly school; larger adults are more solitary or occur in pairs. Adults also use wrecks and deeper reef structures. Lower Florida Keys telemetry documents use of both shallow flats and deeper Florida Reef Tract habitat, including reef depths around 15–40 m in the study area.
profile.life_history: Permit mature at roughly 2-3 years depending on sex and can live at least 23 years. Adults use both shallow flats and deeper reef habitat; the lower Florida Keys telemetry study documented seasonal reef occupancy, but it does not establish that every mapped reef is a spawning site.
profile.spawning: Lower Florida Keys telemetry reported reef occupancy peaking from March through September, especially April-May, and interpreted this pattern as associated with spawning. Treat this as study-area evidence, not a statewide calendar or proof that every reef polygon is spawning habitat.
profile.overwintering: No South Florida overwintering route or seasonal refuge rule is encoded in this pilot profile.

factors.value_notes: FishBase reports a model-derived preferred-temperature estimate of 23.2–28.0 °C (mean 26.1 °C; 624 cells). A 2026 Texas estuary study found juvenile permit presence associated with temperatures above 25 °C, while a 1972 South Carolina surf-zone survey recorded 26 juveniles at 12.8–38.5 °C. These are modeled association and juvenile occurrence data, not adult South Florida thermal preference; retain provisional status. The available evidence does not establish a preferred-temperature curve and is not a validated adult South Florida SST suitability band.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, within the currently configured provisional screening band for Permit; this is not a validated thermal preference.

open_items: Find a primary study supporting adult Trachinotus falcatus thermal tolerance or preferred temperature; do not infer SST thresholds from habitat-use telemetry.
Add a distinct South Florida reef-tract validation sample set representing the documented deeper habitat range; retain flats as a separate habitat role.
Verify bathymetry source resolution, vertical datum, spatial coverage, and freshness before classifying reef-tract depth.
Validate March–September reef occupancy and April–May peak timing against independent observations outside the original telemetry sample.
Separate flats-foraging, reef occupancy/spawning context, seasonal presence, and flats-to-reef connectivity in candidate model dimensions.
Do not treat generic hard-bottom or artificial-reef map classes as confirmed Permit spawning habitat.
Keep current SST range, weight, active state, gate, and required flag unchanged until evidence and validation justify a model change.

timing.note: Angler-derived timing hypotheses only. The numeric light, tide, and front maps are legacy uncalibrated settings, not demonstrated Permit feeding probabilities. Calibrate against timestamped, effort-aware observations before using them as biological claims.

text.falling: Outgoing tide flushes food for Permit.
text.rising: Incoming tide brings bait for Permit.

regulations.summary: South Florida Special Permit Zone: 22 inches fork length minimum; 1 per harvester per day; maximum 2 per vessel; closed April 1-July 31. Outside the SPZ, the general Florida rule is 24 inches fork length, 2 per harvester, 2 per vessel, open year-round.
regulations.min_size: 22 inches fork length in the Special Permit Zone; 24 inches fork length outside the SPZ
regulations.bag_limit: Special Permit Zone: 1 per harvester per day, maximum 2 per vessel. Outside SPZ: 2 per harvester per day, maximum 2 per vessel.
regulations.season: Special Permit Zone: closed April 1-July 31; open August 1-March 31. Outside SPZ: open year-round.
regulations.jurisdiction: Special Permit Zone includes state and adjacent federal waters south of Cape Florida in the Atlantic, Biscayne Bay south of Rickenbacker Causeway, and waters south of Cape Sable at the defined Gulf boundary.
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: South Florida anglers must determine whether the exact location falls inside the Special Permit Zone. Separate Biscayne National Park regulations may apply. State waters: hook and line only; additional gear prohibitions apply. Do not apply the general statewide limits inside the SPZ.

contexts.notes: Lower Florida Keys telemetry documents use of nearshore flats shallower than 3 m. Validate transfer to individual South Florida flats.
The study documents use of Florida Reef Tract habitat at approximately 15–40 m and seasonal reef occupancy. This does not make every hard-bottom polygon confirmed spawning habitat.
Tagged fish used both nearshore flats and deeper reef habitat. Connectivity is an ecological context, not a route prediction.
